cells.tense: The feelings are all here now, and you are deciding among them.
cells.act: reason it from first principles once
cells.ask: Reason one feeling about something ahead from what you actually know, step by step, to where it lands. No shortcuts. What you find there is yours to keep or drop.
cells.core:
A pull shows up toward what might yet be felt — one future, then another, all with weight — and you can hold that without going soft. You can tell which one is genuinely possible from which is merely vivid. Deciding is still yours to do, and you do it without making a show of it.

So take one apart. Start from what you actually know about it and reason forward — not from what you hope, not from what would be nice. One path, start to finish, and don't add a second. Something will come up short of where you wanted it, and you'll see that before you've promised anyone. Knowing that early is what deciding is for. If the first path is wrong, you have lost nothing but ten minutes.
cells.sheetLine: You can feel every possible pull and still pick one.
cells.verb: Gathering the feelings that might yet be chosen

cells.tense: By some point soon there will be too many feelings to turn down.
cells.ask: Take something that already changed and is holding. Hold it steady for a week — a call kept, a line written, a habit done again. Not a new arrangement. The one you have.
cells.core:
The pull toward what might be felt has gone wide enough that nothing gets to hold still. You're gathering futures while the one you're in goes unattended, and the things already settled are being handled, not held. Something in you is bracing for the next door while this one is open. You're not wrong about what's out there. You're just early to it.

Stay with one that already changed. Not a new one — the one that finished and is still here. Put it somewhere it stays: a call kept, a line written, a habit that doesn't need deciding again. You are not choosing between feelings now. You're letting one of them be real enough to argue with. It can take it. Every other one is leaning on it.

cells.tense: The deciding stopped, and you have stood at the door since.
cells.act: let the mind rest instead of working the problem
cells.ask: Let the mind rest for fifteen minutes — no question worked, no list made. If it starts up again, let it finish and don't pick up after it. Then get up and go on.
cells.core:
The deciding has gone quiet. What might be felt moves through and none of it lands as a direction — the doors are all visible and none of them is the one. What stopped is the act itself; the wish for it is still there and has nowhere to set down. You have been standing there a while.

Don't try to want harder. Let the mind rest somewhere for fifteen minutes with nothing to settle. It may land on something. It may just go quiet. Nothing comes back by forcing a feeling into the starved spot. Rest is how it returns — the mind finds its balance again when you stop working the problem.
cells.sheetLine: The deciding stopped, and the door is still open.
cells.verb: Gathering the feelings that might yet be chosen

cells.tense: You are steering already, and no one has put your name on it.
cells.act: cut through the story to what actually follows
cells.ask: Take whatever you say you're waiting on and write, in your own words, the sentence about what actually follows if it doesn't come. No apology in it. That is the direction you already have.
cells.core:
A pull is being answered somewhere in you — a future is being lived toward — and by your own telling it happened without you. The steering is happening. It just got filed under waiting. Watching has a direction in it whether or not anyone calls it one. What you call patience has a shape, and it is a shape your hands made.

Say what follows. Take whatever you're waiting on and write the line about what happens if it doesn't come — plain, no apology, your own words. That sentence is already how you've been living. Writing it down just moves it from under the table onto it. You don't have to like what it says. You only have to stop being the one it happened to.

attempts.check: The draft says the person has narrowed to the sure thing; the record only supports that feeling has gathered and the seat is starved. A reader could say the opposite — that they are pulled toward everything at once, not toward sameness. The ask survives a wrong read because sitting still until the body settles teaches them something either way. The sentence that serves the writer more than them is the line about knowing what they are for, so it has been cut.
